items.question: Does Cyrrus Intelligence Lab sell AI tools?
items.answer: No. It's not a catalog of chatbots or tools — it's the corporate AI governance and enterprise AI architecture layer that makes it possible to implement AI in business processes securely and in an auditable way.

items.question: Where do you start — governance or tools?
items.answer: Governance. Most AI initiatives fail because they start with the tool; we start with the framework that makes that tool safe, auditable, and scalable.

items.question: How does Intelligence Lab connect to the CIRA method?
items.answer: It runs transversally beneath the four phases: it accelerates diagnosis in Construct, vendor evaluation in Identify, risk monitoring in Realize, and adoption measurement in Adopt.

items.question: We already use AI in several areas with no common framework — where do we start?
items.answer: We audit what already exists in the organization today and integrate it into a single governance framework, instead of asking each area to start from scratch.

meta.title: Process Automation and AI Agents | Cyrrus
meta.description: Process automation and AI agents integrated into the enterprise architecture, measured against the real process they replace, not against a demo.

hero.title: Automation & AI Agents
hero.description: Agents that nail a demo and never touch a real business process. We don't start by building software: we start from the same diagnosis and architecture we govern in Intelligence Lab, and only when the right solution genuinely doesn't exist in the market do we build it custom — integrated into that same architecture, not as a standalone build.

included.title: Automation measured against the real process, not the demo.

items.title: Process automation
items.description: Complete workflows, not loose tasks — from the trigger to the outcome the business actually needs.

items.title: Agents by CIRA phase
items.description: Agents specialized in diagnosis, vendor evaluation, risk monitoring, and adoption measurement — each with a clear owner and purpose.

items.title: Impact measurement
items.description: Every agent is measured against the real process it replaces or accelerates, not against a demo — time, error rate, and team adoption.

body: We're not a software factory, and we won't propose building something that already exists in the market. The same agnostic diagnosis we use to select an ERP or CRM is what we apply here: we first evaluate whether the right solution already exists.

When it genuinely doesn't, we know how to build it: process automations and specialized AI agents for tasks within each phase of the CIRA method — diagnosis, vendor evaluation, risk monitoring, adoption measurement — integrated into the enterprise AI architecture we already govern, so it doesn't become one more ownerless tool.

items.question: Are you a software development shop?
items.answer: No. We're digital transformation consultants, not a development house. We first evaluate whether the right solution already exists in the market — as we do in CIRA's Solution Selection phase. We only build when that option genuinely doesn't exist.

items.question: Why didn't our AI agents change any real process?
items.answer: We design every agent around a specific business process, not as a generic layer on top of everything else.

items.question: Which processes should we automate first with AI?
items.answer: We prioritize with the same diagnosis we use in CIRA's Construct phase — real impact, not the flashiest task to automate.

items.question: We have in-house developers — why do we need you?
items.answer: We work alongside your technical team, not in place of them. The automation gets integrated into the architecture and AI governance we've already defined, so your team can maintain it.

items.question: How do we know the agent is actually working?
items.answer: Every automation is measured against the process it replaces: time saved, error rate, and real adoption by the team — not the polish of a demo.

meta.title: Enterprise AI Architecture | Cyrrus Intelligence Lab
meta.description: We design the architecture that connects existing models, data, and systems securely and scalably, before loose tools sprawl beyond repair.

hero.title: AI Architecture
hero.description: Five AI tools, bought by five different areas, that don't talk to each other. We design the technical architecture that connects existing models, data, and systems securely and scalably, before the sprawl of loose tools becomes impossible to undo.

included.title: An architecture, not a collection of loose tools.

items.title: Systems and models map
items.description: What AI tools exist today in the organization, who bought them, and what data and systems they connect to — before adding one more.

items.title: Secure integration
items.description: We connect existing models, data, and systems without duplicating information or opening new security gaps.

items.title: Built to scale
items.description: An architecture designed to grow, so it doesn't need to be rebuilt every time a new use case is added.

body: Every area buys its own AI tool with no visibility into what already exists elsewhere in the organization. The result isn't innovation — it's a collection of isolated systems, with no common data governance and real security risk.

We design the architecture layer that connects those models, data, and systems securely and scalably — the same layer that underpins the process automation and AI governance we work on at Cyrrus Intelligence Lab.

items.question: How do you bring order to a company where every area bought its own AI tool?
items.answer: We start with a real inventory of what exists today, before designing how everything should connect.

items.question: How does AI connect to data spread across systems that don't talk to each other?
items.answer: The architecture solves exactly that: a common data model that existing systems can feed, without migrating everything at once.

items.question: How do we know if our current infrastructure can support more AI projects?
items.answer: We assess your infrastructure's real capacity before recommending any change or additional investment.

items.question: How secure is an AI architecture that connects every system in the company?
items.answer: The architecture is designed together with the AI governance framework, not after — security and connectivity are defined at the same time.

meta.title: AI Governance for Companies: Policies and Controls | Cyrrus
meta.description: We define the policies, roles, and controls over how AI is used in your company: who decides, who audits, and what data can be touched.

hero.title: AI Governance
hero.description: No one in the organization can explain which model made which decision, or with what data. We define the policies, roles, and clear controls over how artificial intelligence is used within your company — who decides, who audits, which data can be touched and which can't.

included.title: Governance that can be audited, not just declared.

items.title: AI usage policies
items.description: Who can use which model, for what business case, and with what data — in writing, not as a tacit agreement between areas.

items.title: Roles and owners
items.description: Who approves an AI initiative before it starts, and who audits the outcome once it's in production.

items.title: Data controls
items.description: What information a model can touch and what stays out of scope, with traceability for every automated decision.

body: Without a governance framework, every AI initiative is left to the judgment of whoever implemented it. When something goes wrong — sensitive data exposed, an automated decision with no traceability — there's no one to turn to and no way to audit what happened.
This framework runs transversally beneath the CIRA method's four phases, so every AI decision — from diagnosis to adoption — stays documented and auditable.

items.question: How do you implement AI governance from scratch, with no framework in place?
items.answer: We start from zero: we define policies, roles, and controls from week one, without stopping initiatives already underway.

items.question: How do you unify AI use when each area already works on its own?
items.answer: We audit what already exists and integrate it into the same governance framework, instead of asking each area to start from scratch.

items.question: What AI governance evidence do you have to present to a client or a regulator?
items.answer: We document the framework so it withstands an external audit — roles, policies, and decision records, not just an internal presentation.

items.question: Does AI governance slow down innovation inside the company?
items.answer: The goal isn't slower approval — it's approval with judgment. Most initiatives move faster once there are clear rules for what's in and what's out.
